clue.text: Carriage enclosure in Irish county

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for enclosure sits inside the county's name

parts.note: Clare is a county on the west coast of Ireland
enc. is the abbreviation written at the foot of a letter to mark an enclosure

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage kept in a paddock somewhere in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' looks like a field or pen, but it is the letter-writer's abbreviation ENC.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse carriage, named after the Duke of Clarence.

clue.text: River swallows up golf drive

indicators.note: the river's name takes the letter for golf down inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A river engulfs a golfer's long tee shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' reads as a golf shot, but it is the definition in its sense of impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a strong inner impulse or desire, as is an urge.

clue.text: Sleazy soprano cheated, winning gold

indicators.note: winning is read as taking in or gaining, so the gold goes inside the other letters

parts.note: did is slang for cheated, as in 'he did me out of a tenner'
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A seedy singer cheated her way to a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' suggests a prize, but here it means taking in, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sordid is morally squalid and dishonourable, in the way a sleazy affair is.

clue.text: Typically a South American university call centre

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A call centre at a South American university is, as you might expect, entirely typical.
explanation.definitionFit: Typically means in the normal way, which is what the phrase meaning in the customary manner says.

clue.text: Female leaves, getting lost as expected

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for female is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: going off course is straying from the route, getting lost

explanation.surface: A woman walks off and loses her way, just as everyone predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' could be foliage, but it is the deletion signal: one F goes from OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning naturally or certainly, things turning out as anticipated.

clue.text: Triumphant Queen's broadcast to some

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, and to some listeners the two words sound the same

parts.note: Victoria was the British queen from 1837 to 1901, so the possessive is Victoria's

explanation.surface: A victorious monarch's address goes out over the airwaves to a limited audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some' admits that the sound match depends on accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphant and the answer are synonyms, both meaning having won.

clue.text: Coins are suspended in church

indicators.note: in places the verb inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
things that hang are suspended from above

explanation.surface: Coins dangle as decorations in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins are what we call small money in the pocket, the sense of the word in 'have you any spare'.

clue.text: Fine left troops in Gulf with debts

indicators.note: in puts the left and troops letters inside the Gulf-plus-debts letters

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO alphabet; here the gulf letter stands for G
IOUs are written promises to repay, so debts
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed in the Gulf, saddled with debts, are told everything is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorious weather is fine weather; both words describe something splendid or very pleasant.

clue.text: Start struggle to seize Richard's crown

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the struggle word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a fight is a struggle

indicators.note: a crown sits on top, so the crown of the name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A battle begins to snatch King Richard's crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a verb meaning begin; it is the noun, a sudden jump of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden shock or scare, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Correct time to show regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret something

explanation.surface: The right moment has come to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and the answer are synonyms in the sense of accurate or right.

clue.text: New temporary accommodation after club's unrest

indicators.note: after places the club first and the new and accommodation letters behind it

parts.note: a disco is a night club; the 's reads as 'club is'
a tent is temporary shelter, as at a festival

explanation.surface: Fresh tented accommodation outside a night club stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction among people, which is what unrest describes.

clue.text: A foreign youth rounds Cape in the raw

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, so the foreign article and youth together surround the cape letter

parts.note: un is French for a, so a foreign 'a'
a lad is a youth
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A young foreign lad sails around a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an idiom for naked, and unclad means wearing no clothes.

clue.text: Lusty social complex hosts six from the States

indicators.note: hosts means holds as a guest, so the rearranged letters contain the numeral
complex means tangled, so the letters of social are rearranged

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An American social club with a lustful reputation houses six guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' gives the rearrangement LASCIO, which 'hosts' the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascivious means showing strong sexual desire, which is what lusty suggests here.

clue.text: Scottish town didn't at first like clothes on line

parts.note: Airdrie is a town in North Lanarkshire, east of Glasgow

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: In a Scottish town the washing on the line didn't dry at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' suggests fondness but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing hung on a line dries in the open air, so it is dried by the air.

clue.text: Drink with king eating first of rather small nuts

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the drink and king letters contain the others

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A drinking king munches on some rather small nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the snack the king is eating; it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for crazy, and berserk means wildly out of control.

clue.text: Long grass on course is hard and rather uneven

parts.note: on a golf course the rough is the long grass beside the fairway
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The long grass on the golf course is tough going and bumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: The -ish ending means somewhat, so somewhat rough is rather uneven.

clue.text: Buckles primarily designed exclusively for M&S

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: Marks and Spencer, the British high-street store, written as the letters M and S

explanation.surface: Belt buckles designed only for Marks and Spencer, the British high-street store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckles' looks like a noun for belt fastenings; it is a verb, bends out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle something is to twist or warp it out of shape, the same as to deform it.

clue.text: Assassin beat up first woman twice

indicators.note: first puts the reversed beat ahead of the rest
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to drum is to beat

indicators.note: twice means the letters for woman appear two times

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen, taken here as a woman

explanation.surface: A hitman beat up his first woman, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat up' looks like a single violent phrase; 'beat' is DRUM and 'up' reverses it to MURD.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is someone who kills, especially a public figure, so a killer by another name.

clue.text: Discredit English mob briefly upset about lines

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed letters go round the lines
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the Mafia is the mob of organised crime
L is a line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An English gang, upset about the lines written about them, sees its reputation damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns the trimmed gang name after E around, giving IFAME; 'about' opens it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is a bad reputation, and discredit is loss of good name, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Young Henry hosts quite posh set

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so the young prince's name contains the other letters

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's history plays
a bit means quite, as in 'a bit cold'
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: The young prince entertains a rather upper-class crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a social group at the end; it is the adjective meaning fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Set in one's ways describes fixed routine, and habitual means done by regular custom.

clue.text: Ancient silver lode plundered

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: plundered means ransacked, so the letters of lode are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old seam of silver ore has been looted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, of long standing, which the hyphenated phrase also means.

clue.text: Win over Germany is a rare miracle for starters

parts.note: D is Germany's international vehicle code, from Deutschland

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A victory against Germany would be something of a rare miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win over' looks like a sports result; it means charm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to charm away their hostility, which is what winning them over does.

clue.text: Greens tipped to control large city built on oil

indicators.note: controlling means holding, so the reversed greens contain the letter for large
tipped means overturned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a salad is a dish of greens

explanation.surface: Tipping the salad bowl over to keep a large city's oil in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas in Texas grew rich on the oil industry, the setting of the TV soap of that name.

clue.text: Pretty messy dull fight with close finish

indicators.note: messy means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rather messy, dull fight ends in a close finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like 'rather' modifying messy; it is the definition, meaning lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean charming or pleasing to look at, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Cut down a lot

definitions.meaning: killed, the past tense of slay

explanation.surface: Reduced a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the past tense of slay, to cut down, and an informal noun for a large quantity.

clue.text: Person has little money by end of April

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of little value

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is short of cash by the end of April.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul is used for an individual person, as in 'not a soul was there'.

clue.text: Swarms could possibly start to shrink

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Swarms of insects could perhaps begin to dwindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swarms' reads as a verb but is the plural noun here: masses of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds of insects are dense masses of them, the same as swarms.

clue.text: Middle East bound to cut limits of arms amounts

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so the bound word sits between the outer letters
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: bound to means sure to, certain

explanation.surface: The Middle East is set to reduce its arms stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: Measures are quantities such as a measure of whisky, so measured amounts.
